questions.questionText: What does a Gini impurity of 0 at a node mean?
options: The node has no training examples
All examples at that node belong to a single class — it's perfectly pure
questions.correctAnswer: All examples at that node belong to a single class — it's perfectly pure
questions.explanation: Gini impurity measures class mixing; 0 means every example in that group shares the same label.

questions.questionText: An unconstrained decision tree grown to full depth typically:
options: Achieves near-perfect training accuracy but generalizes poorly (overfits)
Cannot be trained on numeric features
questions.correctAnswer: Achieves near-perfect training accuracy but generalizes poorly (overfits)
questions.explanation: Without limits like max_depth or min_samples_leaf, the tree keeps splitting until it memorizes the training set, including its noise.

questions.questionText: What kind of decision boundary can a decision tree learn that linear/logistic regression cannot?
options: None — trees are also restricted to straight-line boundaries
Arbitrary, non-linear, axis-aligned boundaries made of rectangular regions
Only boundaries with exactly two splits
questions.correctAnswer: Arbitrary, non-linear, axis-aligned boundaries made of rectangular regions
questions.explanation: Because each split is an independent if/else threshold on one feature, a tree can carve up feature space into non-linear, rectangular regions that a single linear boundary can't represent.
